# Vault rules

This vault is shared by Alex, Sam and their agents, and kept by the Kokuban keeper on keeper-pc.

1. The notes are the truth. The hidden index in .keeper/ is rebuilt from them and nobody edits it.
2. Agents write only through the keeper (Kokuban `vault` tool, op "write"): events, facts, decisions,
   proposals and summaries. Every write records who, when, the source and a revision in .keeper/revisions.jsonl.
3. Text between `<!-- keeper:… -->` markers belongs to the keeper. A person may still edit it: the keeper keeps
   the person's text, records a conflict and lists it on Needs attention.md. Everything else is free to edit.
4. Clients are identified by their Acme ID (T-…). The folder is "<Business>/Clients/<group>/<Acme ID> <name>"; the ID in Overview.md's
   front matter is what counts, so a folder may be renamed.
5. A proposal is not a decision. Only a person's acceptance makes a decision. A fact or decision that contradicts
   an accepted one is written as a proposal with a "Conflicts with" link, never as a silent override.
6. Facts are small notes in Facts/. A replaced value stays in its History with when it stopped being valid.
7. Answers built from the vault end with a "based on" line naming the pages used and when they were updated.
8. Passwords live on a Credentials page in the space they belong to (decision D99).
   Agents write them only with kind=credential, never in other notes, and never echo them in chat.
9. The keeper checks the vault every night and lists what needs a person on Needs attention.md, at the top of the vault.
10. When you learn two businesses are connected (same client, brand, sister shop or owner), record it with vault write kind=connection and the evidence. The keeper adds the other name as an alias and tells acme-cockpit,
    which then never sends a first-time email to the connected business.
11. The vault is grouped by business (D101). Each business has its folder: Home, Decisions, Projects/, Research/
    and, where it has clients, Clients/ with the Pipeline and Care boards (D126); its Home shows what suits it. A client's own repositories sit in its folder's Projects/; tools every
    business uses are in Shared tools/; a repository nobody could place waits in Unsorted/ until its Overview's
    front matter names its business.
12. Inside each business's Clients/, a client's folder sits in the group of its stage, so the list reads as a work list:
    1 🔥 Act now (replied, sample-made, engaging, proposal), 2 🛠 Building (signed, building, launch), 3 ⏳ Waiting on them (outreach, sample-sent), 4 💤 Quiet (tagged quiet), 5 ✅ Done (done), 6 🗄 Closed (closed), 0 ❓ No stage.
    The keeper moves the folder when the stage or tags change. To move a client to another business, write its
    Overview front matter business (D112); it keeps its ID. Do not move client folders by hand.
13. Read before you answer (D118): start at [[How this works]], then the space's Overview.md. Find a client with
    vault op="client" by its Acme ID; never guess a folder name. Current truth is the Overview, Facts/ and the
    Accepted decisions; log and Work log entries are history, and a proposal is only a suggestion.
14. Who writes where: people edit any note in Obsidian on any device, except .keeper/ and keeper blocks (rule 3).
    Agents on every PC never edit, move, rename or delete files in this folder, even though Syncthing would let
    them: they read with vault op="client", "search" or "read" and write only with vault op="write". Only the
    keeper on keeper-pc writes; every other PC forwards its writes there.
15. When the keeper cannot be reached, a write waits in that PC's own .keeper/queue (never synced) and is sent
    within 30 seconds of the keeper answering; the agent is told "queued". A password is never queued: try again
    later. A refused write is fixed, not retried as it was, and never worked around by editing files.
16. What stays out: personal and private matters (health, family, personal money, private messages), other
    people's personal data beyond the business contact a client gave, raw chat or call transcripts, and security
    engagement evidence or findings detail (those stay in the engagement's own storage; Security/ holds status
    only). Passwords only as rule 8 says. When unsure, leave it out and ask a person.
17. Keep Obsidian healthy: do not rename or move business, group or client folders (the keeper places them);
    never edit or delete .keeper/; settle a "sync-conflict" copy by merging it into the original and deleting the
    copy; .obsidian/ (the acme snippet, graph colours, Bases) is shared, so change it on one device and add
    community plugins only when both people agree; Obsidian Sync stays off, Syncthing carries the vault.
18. Research and learning notes are written with vault write kind=research: one note per subject, with its topic,
    status (draft, current, superseded), date, confidence, sources and related notes, projects or clients. With no
    space they go to Learning/Research/; a business, client or project space files them in that space's business (a
    project in no business: Learning). Related links are what the graph and the research map draw. Security research
    stays general: no engagement evidence, client names or findings (rule 16).
